architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented Famulor as a redirect-based automation app following the established 'link-as-an-app' template pattern used by other automation apps like Telli, Framer, and Cron
architecture_decisions.rationale: The codebase has a well-defined pattern for apps that don't require complex OAuth flows but instead redirect users to external services. This approach minimizes implementation complexity while maintaining consistency with existing integrations. The '__template': 'link-as-an-app' in config.json confirms this pattern usage.
alternatives_considered: Full OAuth integration with credential storage
Custom API endpoints for bidirectional communication

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created minimal API handlers that use the existing createDefaultInstallation utility and declarative handler pattern
architecture_decisions.rationale: Leveraging the established AppDeclarativeHandler type and createDefaultInstallation function ensures type safety and consistency with other app store integrations. The add.ts handler follows the same structure as other redirect apps, focusing only on the redirect URL and credential creation without custom business logic.
alternatives_considered: Custom API endpoints with unique business logic
Direct database operations bypassing existing utilities
Server-side rendering components for the integration flow

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated auto-generated registry files (apps.metadata.generated.ts, apps.server.generated.ts, redirect-apps.generated.ts) to include Famulor in the app store listings
architecture_decisions.rationale: The codebase uses generated files to maintain a centralized registry of all apps. This ensures the UI can discover and render Famulor alongside other apps without manual component updates. The generation system automatically picks up new app directories with proper config.json files.
alternatives_considered: Manual updates to component imports throughout the codebase
Dynamic runtime discovery of app directories
Custom registration system separate from existing generators

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Included comprehensive DESCRIPTION.md with marketing content and multiple demo images, plus proper SVG icon for dark theme
architecture_decisions.rationale: Following the established pattern for app store listings ensures consistent user experience. The DESCRIPTION.md uses the same frontmatter structure (--- items: [...] ---) as other apps. The SVG icon is optimized with base64 encoding for performance and includes proper viewBox and preserveAspectRatio attributes.
alternatives_considered: Minimal documentation with just basic functionality
External image hosting instead of bundled assets
PNG icons instead of SVG for simplicity

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added workspace dependencies to @calcom/lib and @calcom/types in package.json without external npm dependencies
architecture_decisions.rationale: Using workspace:* dependencies ensures version consistency across the monorepo and avoids dependency conflicts. The minimal dependencies reflect that this is a simple redirect app without complex functionality requiring additional packages.
alternatives_considered: Adding external npm packages for Famulor-specific functionality
Creating shared dependencies with other automation apps
Bundling all dependencies in the main package.json

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Used TypeScript with proper type imports from @calcom/types and followed the AppDeclarativeHandler interface
architecture_decisions.rationale: Maintaining full type safety ensures compile-time error checking and better developer experience. The handler explicitly defines appType, variant, slug, and other required properties that the TypeScript compiler can validate against the existing type definitions.
alternatives_considered: Custom type definitions separate from existing patterns

implementation_summary:
The Famulor app integration was implemented as a redirect-based automation app following Cal.com's established patterns for external service integrations. The approach leverages the existing 'link-as-an-app' template, which is designed for services that handle authentication and configuration on their own platforms rather than through Cal.com's OAuth flow.

The implementation creates a complete app directory structure under packages/app-store/famulor/ with all necessary configuration files, API handlers, and static assets. The config.json defines Famulor as an automation app with type 'famulor_automation', ensuring it appears in the correct category in the app store. The API handler uses the declarative pattern established by other redirect apps, simply redirecting users to Famulor's documentation page while creating a minimal credential record in Cal.com's database.

Key design decisions include using the existing generated file system for app discovery, maintaining type safety through proper TypeScript interfaces, and providing comprehensive documentation and marketing assets to match the quality of other app store listings. The implementation is minimal yet complete, adding Famulor to all the necessary registries (metadata, server handlers, redirect apps) without modifying any core application logic.

The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing codebase by following established conventions for app store integrations. The use of workspace dependencies ensures version consistency, and the inclusion in yarn.lock reflects proper monorepo dependency management. This implementation allows users to discover and 'install' Famulor from the Cal.com app store, initiating a redirect to Famulor's platform where the actual integration configuration occurs.
